page: Best practices for Hono application architecture and patterns. Avoid Ruby on Rails-like controllers; write handlers directly inline for better type inference. Use factory.createHandlers() from hono/factory for controller pattern if needed. Use app.route() for larger applications to modularize endpoints. RPC type inference via export type AppType = typeof app and hc<AppType>(). HEAD request handling: automatic HEAD-to-GET conversion with body stripping before route matching; use GET routes, middleware for HEAD-specific logic; cannot override with dedicated HEAD or on() handlers. Performance: detect HEAD in middleware to skip expensive operations. Testing: verify both GET and HEAD responses have matching status and headers. Consistent across all Hono runtimes. What middleware patterns work with HEAD?

sections.manifest: Avoid creating Ruby on Rails-like controllers for type inference issues. Problem: path parameters in separated controller functions cannot infer types without complex generics. Solution: write handlers directly after path definitions inline. Example: app.get('/books/:id', (c) => {...}) allows c.req.param('id') type inference. Benefit: simpler code, better type safety. Questions: Why avoid controllers? How do inline handlers improve types? What's the difference in type inference?

factory.createHandlers() in hono/factory provides RoR-like controller pattern with correct type inference. Import: createFactory from 'hono/factory'. Creates: createMiddleware(), createHandlers(). createHandlers() accepts middleware and final handler returning typed response. Usage: factory = createFactory(), middleware = factory.createMiddleware(), handlers = factory.createHandlers(logger(), middleware, handler), app.get('/api', ...handlers). Benefits: RoR pattern with TypeScript support. Questions: How do I use factory pattern? What's the syntax for createHandlers()? How do I combine middleware with handlers?

Use app.route() for modularity in larger applications without controllers. Pattern: create separate files (authors.ts, books.ts) with Hono instances and routes, export default app. Main index.ts imports and mounts: app.route('/authors', authors), app.route('/books', books). For RPC: chain route definitions as .get(...).post(...).get(...), export type AppType = typeof app. Client: hc<AppType>('url') gets correct typing. Reference: /docs/guides/rpc#using-rpc-with-larger-applications. Questions: How do I separate route files? How do I mount sub-apps? How do I export types for RPC? What's the chaining pattern?

HEAD request handling: Hono automatically converts HEAD to GET before route matching, strips response body. Do: use GET routes (automatically handles HEAD), use middleware to detect c.req.method === 'HEAD'. Don't: create dedicated HEAD handlers via app.head() or app.on('HEAD'), won't be called. Performance: avoid expensive operations in GET if many HEAD requests; use middleware to skip body generation; cache headers work identically; middleware like compression skip HEAD automatically. Testing: test both GET and HEAD; verify matching status, headers, and null body. Behavior consistent across Cloudflare Workers, Deno, Bun, Node.js. Consideration: use different endpoints if needing completely different HEAD vs GET logic. Questions: How does HEAD request handling work? Do I need dedicated HEAD handlers? How do I optimize HEAD performance? What headers apply to HEAD requests?
